normal.definition: The deep, almost private satisfaction of peeling the protective film off a brand-new screen in one clean pull.
normal.example: Mit einem leisen Seufzer genoss sie die Schutzfolienabziehfreude. (With a quiet sigh, she savored the joy of peeling off the screen film.)

normal.definition: The exact sip at which a cup of coffee goes from pleasantly warm to disappointingly lukewarm.
normal.example: Ich habe den Kaffeekipppunkt wieder verpasst. (I missed the coffee tipping point again.)

normal.definition: The rising dread, during the countdown to a group photo, that you will be the one person caught mid-blink.
normal.example: „Drei, zwei…“ – und schon packte ihn die Gruppenfotoblinzelangst. ("Three, two…" – and the group-photo blink dread took hold of him.)

normal.definition: The thin, brittle patience reserved for a progress bar stuck at 99%.
normal.example: Meine Ladebalkengeduld ist heute aufgebraucht. (My loading-bar patience is used up today.)

long.definition: The quiet, unspoken solidarity among participants of an early Monday video call who have all, without discussion, decided to leave their cameras off. Nobody mentions it, nobody needs to; the grid of initials says everything, and for a brief moment a group of near-strangers is united by the shared knowledge that none of them has brushed their hair.
long.example: Als der Chef fragte, ob jemand die Kamera einschalten könne, herrschte nur Schweigen – ein perfektes Montagmorgenbesprechungskameraeinschaltverweigerungsgemeinschaftsgefühl. (When the boss asked whether anyone could turn on their camera, there was only silence – a perfect Monday-morning-meeting camera-refusal solidarity.)

refusal.definition: The hollow feeling of having typed something crude into a word generator, only to be handed a dictionary entry about yourself.
refusal.example: Nach dem dritten Versuch spürte er nur noch Provokationsleere. (After the third attempt, he felt only the emptiness of provocation.)
